catalog_quote: There are four phonetic tones (allotones): high, low, falling, and rising ... Falling and rising tones are heavily restricted in environment, as described below. The high and low tones pattern in a pitch accent system (contra Alidou (1988:33), who claims Dazaga has two tonemes, a high and a low ...). The high tone(s) is part of the underlying form of a word, and the low tone is assigned afterward, by default, to any unassociated vowels. No words occur in my data in which all tones are low ... The “obligatoriness” property requires that every word have at least one accented syllable, or high tone; the “culminativity” property requires that every word have only one accented syllable. These typical properties are found in Dazaga, if “culminativity” is extended to require only one accented syllable or series of syllables per word. sweep_summary: Two works with stress in the title, both by V. A. Dybo on 'Tubu' = Lukas 1953's Kashirda (Keshirda) Daza, the same dialect as the catalog's source Walters 2015. (1) Dybo 1987 (100-pp chapter, Russian; Glottolog ref) was found open on inslav.ru, downloaded, scanned (image-only 2-up scan; 300 dpi for the key pages, 200 dpi elsewhere) and read: preliminary contour rule p. 469 'ударение ставится на первый высокий тон словоформы' (stress on the first high tone of the word-form; falling = high), conclusion p. 553 (an earlier reading distribution linked to tone schemes by a Balto-Slavic-type contour rule; tones fading; system intermediate between tone and paradigmatic accent). (2) Dybo 1994 (English, St. Petersburg Journal of African Studies, two parts 2: 29-50 and 3: 27-44 per Dybo's own bibliography) has no open copy anywhere located; but its Russian text, Dybo 1995 MLJ 1: 236-279 (same work per Dybo's bibliography item 105), was downloaded from inslav.ru and read in full: p. 269 final rule 'акцент.. падает.. на первый слог с высоким тоном', p. 240 verbs form barytone (H root) vs oxytone (L root) accent types, p. 239 quotes Lukas 1953: 7 verbatim on the 'starker Akzent (Druck)'. Both refine rather than contradict the catalog's tonal / pitch accent coding (Walters 2015): they supply a stress statement Walters lacks -- dynamic stress predictable as the first H-toned syllable, i.e. the left edge of Walters's obligatory contiguous H-span -- while keeping placement tone-driven and lexically distributed. Recommended: keep Walters 2015 as deciding source, add Dybo 1987: 469/553 and Dybo 1995: 240, 269 as supporting sources with the first-H stress rule; Lukas 1953: 7-8 (De Gruyter DOI 10.1515/9783112766194, paywalled) remains the primary data source worth acquiring. All files under ( and updated). discovery used direct downloads of inslav.ru, archive.org, Crossref and Semantic Scholar APIs.

new_statements.quote: Внутренняя реконструкция (анализ системы в терминах акцентуационных валентностей и сравнение результатов с тоновыми схемами III глагольной группы), подтверждаемая непосредственным сравнением с тонами канури, позволяет установить, что акцент в тубу регулируется контурным правилом балто-славянского типа, т.е. акцент падает на начало первой последовательности морфем (соответственно, слогов) высшей валентности, иначе говоря, на первый слог с высоким тоном (соответственно, с восходящим или нисходящим тоном, которые приравниваются в контурном правиле к высокому).
new_statements.translation: Internal reconstruction (analysis of the system in terms of accentual valencies and comparison of the results with the tone schemes of verb group III), confirmed by direct comparison with the tones of Kanuri, allows us to establish that accent in Tubu is governed by a contour rule of the Balto-Slavic type, i.e. the accent falls on the beginning of the first sequence of morphemes (correspondingly, syllables) of higher valency -- in other words, on the first syllable with high tone (or with rising or falling tone, which the contour rule treats as high).
new_statements.citation: Dybo, V. A. 1995. Akcentuacionnye processy v jazykakh gruppy teda-kanuri i problema proiskhozhdenija paradigmaticheskikh akcentnykh sistem. Moskovskij lingvisticheskij zhurnal 1: 236-279 (Russian text of Dybo 1994, St. Petersburg Journal of African Studies 2: 29-50; 3: 27-44). Companion: Dybo 1987, Afrikanskoe istoricheskoe jazykoznanie 458-557, p. 469.
new_statements.locator: p. 269 (PDF p. 18, right half), closing paragraph of the Tubu analysis; cf. p. 240 (two accent types) and Dybo 1987: 469 (preliminary rule, underlined) and 553 (conclusion)
new_statements.reading: Dybo, working from the stress-marked verb paradigms in Lukas 1953 (Kashirda/Keshirda Daza -- the same dialect Walters 2015 describes), finds that Tubu/Dazaga has a dynamic stress (Lukas's 'starker Akzent (Druck)') whose position is fully predictable from tone: it falls on the first high-toned syllable of the word-form, falling and rising tones counting as high. Verbs split into barytona (H root, root stress) and oxytona (L root, ending stress); tone classes of preformatives are lexical. He characterises the system as tone in a 'fading' state, transitional between a classical tone system and a paradigmatic-accent system (1987: 554). This is consistent with, and adds a stress rule to, Walters's pitch accent analysis (one obligatory contiguous H-span per word; Dybo's an earlier reading is the left edge of that span). It does not turn Dazaga into a positional or weight-sensitive stress language: placement is tone-conditioned and lexically distributed, so the catalog's tonal/pitch accent coding stands, with 'stress = first H syllable (Dybo 1987/1995, from Lukas 1953)' as a refinement.

audit.reasoning: Quote check: both the 'quote' and 'the domain quotation' passages and the fn. 28 exception are verbatim in the Walters 2015 PDF we hold at Section 3.4, printed pp. 34-35, as the locator says. Deciding source: a 2015 MA-thesis grammar by the author of the only modern reference grammar (Brill 2016), open text, with tonal minimal triplets and an explicit obligatoriness/culminativity argument; no mention of stress anywhere in the work. Every earlier description Walters cites (Lukas 1953, Amani 1986, Alidou 1988, Wolff & Alidou 1989, Wolff 1991) treats Dazaga as tonal, disagreeing only on the number of tonemes, so the 'tonal / no stress rule' coding is not at risk. WALS has no prosody values for Tubu. Better sources not yet obtained are either the paywalled published version of the same work or older print-only tone articles (Wolff 1991, Dybo 1987) that could refine the tone-vs-pitch accent characterisation but would not

sources.quote: Уже на данном этапе сравнения становится ясным, что правило, которым регулируется постановка акцента в словоформе, теснейшим образом связано с тональной схемой этой словоформы. Предварительно контурное правило можно сформулировать следующим образом: ударение ставится на первый высокий тон словоформы, при этом нисходящий тон в данном правиле приравнивается высокому. [p. 469] ... Итак, выше было показано, что иктусное распределение в тубу, образующее акцентные схемы слов, поразительно напоминающие акцентные парадигмы в языках "парадигматического акцента", связано при помощи контурного правила "балто-славянского типа" с тоновыми схемами этого языка. [p. 553]

sources.quote: Die Tubusprache besitzt einen starken Akzent (Druck), der der Sprache einen energischen Charakter verleiht. In welcher Weise der Akzent rhythmisch im Satz verteilt wird, bedarf näherer Untersuchung. Der Ton spielt auch im Tubu eine nicht zu unterschätzende Rolle. ... eine große Anzahl von Verbalwurzeln ist hoch- bzw. tieftonig, wodurch die Tonfolgen der Verbalformen bestimmt werden und regelmäßige Tonschemata entstehen [Lukas 1953, S. 7].
sources.note: Foundational Tubu grammar; pp. 7-8 treat tone (cited by Walters). Would show whether the older literature ever described a word accent ('Akzent') rather than tone.
